cases.name: Jennifer Fulford
cases.about: She was a caretaker for a family and had the nickname "Jenny Poppins." "The man we suspect took her life, she probably would've done anything to help him out, just like she helped out other people," said Robert Fulford in talking about his wife. "It's just so indescribable … she was just so full of life."
cases.narrative: He duct taped her face and suffocated her, and stabbed her multiple times, leaving her body in a field. Her wrists and ankles were also reportedly bound.

cases.name: Merrie Garcia Berrios
cases.about: Officials said they received a call from a person who told them a family at The Park Apartments on Park Promenade Drive was being threatened by a man, later identified as Ezequiel Umpierre Placencia, inside the home. At the time, authorities said Placencia, Merrie Garcia Berrios and three children were in the apartment. According to deputies, they were told Placencia would kill "them" if he saw authorities. Officials said it is unclear if Placencia meant he would kill police or those inside the home.

cases.name: Loretta Patrice Harvey
cases.about: Her obituary said, "Loretta Patrice Harvey affectionately known as “Retta”; a beloved mother, daughter, sister, aunt, niece, cousin and friend. Retta accepted Christ at an early age in New York at the family church and later worshipped at Macedonia Missionary Baptist Church in Eatonville, Florida. Retta was a woman of faith who loved spending time with her family and friends.  She loved horror movies and comedy.  She truly enjoyed family bonding during holidays,  sister time chats, brunch, happy hours, game nights, travel, etc.  Retta was a phenomenal hair stylist known to many as “Braids by Lo”.  She recently ventured out and excelled in social media marketing.  Her most recent achievements were becoming a certified sister lock consultant and real estate investor.  We intend to carry that torch in her honor."

cases.name: Rebecca White
cases.about: She worked as a licensed mental health counselor at her own therapy practice, Down to Earth Therapy Solutions.
cases.narrative:
Smith was a registered sex offender who was released from prison in 2022. His parole required that he have "psychological or psychiatric evaluation geared towards someone who has committed a violent and vicious sexual battery and who has a violent anti-social personality disorder."

She had just finished a session with another client at around 9 p.m. local time on Monday, Jan. 19, when Smith arrived at her Orlando office demanding to speak with her. Deputies said Smith then began repeatedly stabbing both White and her client, a man in his 30s. The client was eventually able to call 911, and Smith fled the scene.  Both White and her client, who is expected to survive, were found with stab wounds and transported to a local hospital. The therapist later died from her injuries, while the client, whose identity has not been made public, is expected to survive.
